info.title: Permguard common wire types
info.description: Components shared by every Permguard REST surface: the refusal body, the access gate's denial body and the JWKS served at the key-set endpoints.

class.description: Which kind of thing went wrong; fixes the HTTP status: 400, 409, 404, 503, 500.

code.description: The stable name of the exact condition.

WireError.description: A domain refusal, the same three fields on every wire (`permguard_core::WireError`).
WireError.x-grpc-note: gRPC answers a domain refusal with a status whose metadata carries `permguard-error-class` and `permguard-error-code` (permguard-control-plane wire.rs, permguard-core api.rs); the status message is not the refusal's `message`, and no proto message carries the three fields.

message.description: One sentence for a person, identical for existing and non-existing out-of-scope resources.

WireDenial.description: The access gate's 401 or 403 body: it has no `class`, because the request was never considered.
WireDenial.x-grpc-note: The access gate runs on the HTTP listener only; it has no gRPC body.

kid.description: Which key this is, matching the `kid` a signature names.

kty.description: The key type: `OKP` for the Edwards curves, `EC` for the NIST ones.

crv.description: The curve, when the key type has one.

x.description: The public key itself, base64url without padding.

y.description: The second coordinate, for the key types that have one.

alg.description: The algorithm this key is used with.

use.description: What the key is for; always `sig`.

Jwk.description: One public key as RFC 7517 defines it; the private half is never expressed.
Jwk.x-grpc-note: Carried inside the JSON bytes of `permguard.control.v1.GetKeyRingResponse.jwks`; no proto message models one key.

keys.description: Every key a client may need, in no particular order.

JwkSet.description: The document served at a key-set endpoint.
JwkSet.x-grpc-note: Carried as JSON bytes: `permguard.control.v1.GetKeyRingResponse.jwks` holds the same JWKS document the HTTP endpoint serves; the response message is a bytes wrapper, not a structured JwkSet.
